S9.label: Regional sales view: Products A, B and C across five countries

steps.text: The Sales insights page shows customer purchase orders only. MDM setup requests are a different thing and are kept out of these numbers.

ops.label: Filters
ops.text: These filters steer every chart on the page: country, product, the measure (units, sales value or gross margin) and existing versus new customers. 'Customise page' chooses which blocks appear.

ops.label: Headline
ops.text: Headline numbers. Growth is the change over the last 12 months against the same 12 months a year earlier, shown as a percentage. Green is up, red is down.

ops.label: Map
ops.text: The map comes first. Dot size is the amount, colour is growth, so the biggest and fastest-growing markets stand out across Southeast Asia at a glance.
Picking one country opened the map up to its cities.

ops.label: Malaysia by city
ops.text: Pick Malaysia and the map divides it by city: one hot spot per place, sized by its sales, with each city's share of the country in the table beside it.

ops.label: More detail
ops.text: The three charts below the map (units per month, the growth heatmap and gained or lost) all carry more than the picture: hover any point, bar or cell for the exact figures, and every one follows the filters above.

steps.text: Every graph is customisable. Watch the same data re-cut by measure, by customer group and by comparison.

ops.label: Map
ops.text: One click on 'Sales value' and the headline numbers, map and every chart switch from units to dollars.

ops.label: Heatmap
ops.text: Gross margin uses assumed margins per product, so you can see where profit, not just volume, is growing.

ops.label: Existing only
ops.text: Existing customers only: accounts that bought nothing a year ago are removed, so growth from new customers is separated from growth in what current customers buy.

ops.label: Compare
ops.text: The Compare chart lets you pick any measure, what to compare by and how to draw it.

ops.label: Share
ops.text: By product, shown as a share of the total: which product is taking a growing slice, whatever the overall market does.

ops.label: Index
ops.text: As an index, every product starts at 100, so fast and slow growers compare fairly even when their volumes differ a lot.
Customise page: each block can be switched off, so a regional manager can keep only the map and the heatmap.

ops.label: Actions
ops.text: What should we do? Advice in plain words, ranked by what the business needs: grow sales, keep customers, fix weak spots or spread the risk. It is written from the numbers on this page: growth, forecast accuracy, customers buying less and cross-sell gaps.

steps.text: The forecast explorer predicts the next months for one country and product, and shows how well each model did on months it never saw.

ops.label: Best model
ops.text: The platform pre-selects the model with the lowest error on months it was never shown. Here that is: {value}.

ops.label: Forecast
ops.text: The solid line is history, the dashed line is the forecast and the shaded band is the typical error, measured on hidden months, not guessed.

ops.label: Models
ops.text: Advanced mode draws the other trend models on the same chart, so you can see the best predictive model against today's simpler methods.

ops.label: Linear trend
ops.text: Switching to the plain linear trend changes the line. A straight trend ignores seasons, which is why it is not the one chosen.

ops.label: Comparison
ops.text: Every model was tested on months it never saw. The table shows its average error, lower is better. The traditional flat-average rows are today's method and the yardstick.

ops.label: Observed
ops.text: The observations below the table are written only from these numbers: which model is most accurate, and by how much it beats the traditional average.

ops.label: Holds up?
ops.text: Does the accuracy hold up? The same test is repeated on earlier windows, so the best model is not just one lucky window.

ops.label: Models
ops.text: Each model is explained in plain words: what it does, why choose it and what to watch out for.
Data science also flags customers buying less and customers who could buy more, so people spend time on the right accounts.

ops.label: Rules
ops.text: Next, a rule. The workflow designer decides who approves what. An 'also require' rule adds an approver to any request whenever its condition is true. Here: customers with a credit limit over 20,000 also need the Business Unit Head.
Three questions: who is it for (customers), anything extra (credit limit more than 20000), and who approves.

A customer with a 75,000 credit limit now also goes to the Business Unit Head, which it did not before the rule.
Applying the rule is checked, compared with what it replaces, and written to the audit trail. No file was edited and no code was written.
